newsitem.title: USA: Voters pass measure allowing 3 casinos in Detroit.
newsitem.headline: Voters pass measure allowing 3 casinos in Detroit.

text.p: Michigan voters narrowly approved a measure that allows three casinos to be built in Detroit, gambling proponents said Wednesday.
With 93 percent of the vote counted, the statewide referendum passed 52 percent to 48 percent, said a spokeswoman for the Yes on E Committee, which did not declare victory until 0730/EST Wednesday.
The measure, which was opposed by Michigan Gov. John Engler, authorizes three casinos in cities with more than 800,000 people -- which means Detroit is the only Michigan city to qualify.

Backers, including Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer, say the casinos will generate more than $100 million in tax revenue and stop more than $1 million a day of gambling business that goes across the Detroit River to Windsor, Ontario, each day.

According to the proposal, the casinos would be subject to state regulation and an 18 percent tax. Detroit anti-crime efforts will receive 55 percent of the tax proceeds, with the state's K-12 School Aid Fund receiving 45 percent.

Engler told reporters earlier Wednesday he still does not favor the casino idea, but will follow the law. The governor will be required in the next 60 days to select a five-member bipartisan Gaming Control Board, which will accept casino applications.

Proponents spent heavily, airing ads touting how much money Detroit was losing to Windsor gambling interests. Casino backers were forced to put the issue to a statewide vote after Engler refused last June to allow gambling to spread in the state through the construction of off-reservation Indian casinos.
Anti-gambling advocates were critical of Engler, saying he did not help to raise money and was too quiet in voicing opposition to the measure.
